verdict: OK to lend in Nellore power — but only to generation and equipment/service borrowers with strong private or central counterparties; avoid pure AP Discom receivable exposure until collection cycles shorten.
title: Nellore Power Generation & Distribution: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A power borrower in Nellore turns fuel or sunlight into units, and units into cash only when the offtaker pays.** The district hosts the 2,400 MW Damodaram Sanjeevaiah thermal station at Nelatur, run by APPDCL [3]. Value sits in the PPA and the plant's availability; cash sits in the receivable from the distribution company, not in the meter. Cost structure is fuel plus fixed O&M; pricing power is nil once the tariff order is fixed. So when a proposal lands, check the offtaker's payment record before the plant's PLF. ## What has changed now
**Demand is running hot locally while the state's own tax base is shrinking.** Andhra Pradesh electricity demand is up 18.1% Apr-to-date against India's 9.5% [D], yet AP GST collections are -0.2% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1% [D]. That gap is the whole story: more units sold, less cash in the state's hands. The rating evidence is blunt — AP Discom counterparty risk is flagged as significant, with average collection period over 400 days in FY25 (prior year 351 days) and debtors at Rs 5,020 crore as of June 30, 2025 [10]. Note that source is undated on the page; treat the 400-day figure as the last reported, not current. Local news is thin: APSPDCL has set up control rooms for cyclone-related supply disruption in Nellore and Tirupati [1], and a fire at the Nelatur plant is reported, but that report is from July 2023 and old [3]. ## Where the growth is
**Pursue borrowers whose cash comes from someone other than the state Discom.** Peer results show the money is in operational efficiency and long PPAs: Vedanta Power posted record quarterly sales with EBITDA up 45% sequentially and margins at 14.5% [5], and separately reported 122% EBITDA growth to INR 421 crore on revenue of INR 2,908 crore [6]; Adani Power runs 18.33 GW with 95% of capacity tied to long-term PPAs [7]. In Nellore that means: O&M and balance-of-plant contractors to the thermal station, coal-handling and ash-utilisation units, transmission and substation EPC, and rooftop/captive solar for industrial consumers. Avoid pure play Discom-billed generators and any trader whose sole collateral is an AP Discom receivable. ## How to grow safely
**Structure against the receivable, not the asset.** Take assignment of the PPA and escrow of Discom payments where possible; ICRA's thermal methodology looks at cash collection trends, DSRA availability and working-capital limit utilisation [8]. Ask for the debtor ageing by offtaker and the last twelve months of actual collections — collect from customer where the current collection period is not disclosed. Monthly, take the Discom payment receipt statement, plant availability/PLF, coal or fuel stock days, and the drawing-power statement. ## Early-warning signs
**Watch the state's cash before the plant's.** A widening AP GST decline against India [D] precedes Discom payment stretch. A jump in receivable days beyond the last reported 400 [10], any request to fund interest from a new short-term line, or a cyclone-driven outage at Nelatur [1] should trigger a review of limits and collateral before the next disbursement.
